London, 11<sup>th</sup> March 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**Automobile sales in Brazil** rose in February for the third straight month, helped by government tax breaks that have allowed dealers to lower prices to woo consumers back into showrooms, the national automakers’ association Anfavea said.  Sales of new cars and trucks edged up 1.0 % to 199,400 units, following a 1.5 % increase in January and a 9.4 % surge in December.  On a year-on-year basis, however, sales slipped 0.7 % in February.  Output rose for the second consecutive month, climbing 9.2 % from January to 201,700 units. When compared with Feb 2008, however, production slumped a whopping 20.6 %. 

## _Source:  Reuters_ 

**Mexican automobile production** and exports both fell sharply in February as the U.S. recession continued to hammer the sector, although the sector showed some improvement from a dismal January. Auto exports dropped 44.6 % in February to 77,833 vehicles compared to a year earlier. Exports in January were only about 51,000 units.  Mexico is a major supplier of cars and car parts to the United States and sliding demand from Americans for new cars has hit the country’s auto sector hard. Falling consumer confidence in Mexico has also pinched domestic sales. Auto output fell 38.2 % to 107,547 units in February as many assembly plants cut shifts and imposed temporary shutdowns to reduce stocks. Auto production in February 2008 was 173,887 units. Mexico produced around 2.1 million vehicles in 2008, 1.7 million of them for export. The auto industry offers some of the best paying manufacturing jobs in Mexico and troubles in the sector are hurting the broader Mexican economy. Mexican consumer confidence is at a record low and analysts are increasingly gloomy about the economy’s prospects in 2009. 

## _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**Automotive production in Turkey** fell by 63% to 83,667 units in January-February compared with a year ago as the credit crisis hits domestic sales and exports, the Turkish Automotive Industry Association (OSD) said. Exports fell 61.6% to 69,495 unit in January-February from a year ago.  The OSD said last month it expected 2009 exports and production to fall 25 percent and domestic auto sales to shrink 2%. The OSD predicted that the auto market would start recovering in the final quarter of 2009 under the most optimistic assumption. 

## _Source: Automotive News Europe_ 

**Toyota** is cutting pay and production at its two UK factories by 10%. The cutbacks will affect more than 4,000 workers at its factories in Burnaston and Deesid.  Nissan is cutting 1,200 jobs at its plant in Sunderland, Honda is suspending production at its Swindon factory for several weeks and BMW has cut 850 positions at its Mini factory in Oxford. 

## _Source:  The Guardian_ 

**Platinum Australia** has delayed the finalisation of the bankable-feasibility study of the Kalahari Platinum (Kalplat) project, located in South Africa’s North West province, to Q

2 09.  It is delaying the BFS to consider a number of development options, aimed at reducing capital and operating costs, including increasing cut off grades, reducing stripping ratios, increasing throughput, and considering a potential staged development of the project.
